# linearctl cycle

<!-- Generated by scripts/skill-docs.py from --help; do not edit. -->

## linearctl cycle archive

```
Archive a cycle. One already archived is changed: false. CYCLE is as for cycle
show, within --team.
Changes things: pass --dry-run to preview, --yes to apply.

Usage:
  linearctl cycle archive CYCLE [flags]

Examples:
  linearctl cycle archive 21 --team ENG --dry-run
  linearctl cycle archive 21 --team ENG --yes --json

Flags:
      --dry-run    show what would change; change nothing
  -h, --help       help for archive
      --team KEY   the cycle's team KEY (falls back to LINEARCTL_TEAM, then default-team)
      --yes        apply the change
```

## linearctl cycle create

```
Create a cycle in a team, from --starts-at to --ends-at. Linear numbers it.

--yes requires --id, a UUID you choose, so a rerun can never create a second
cycle: if one with that id exists, it is returned with changed: false.
--dry-run without --id generates one and prints it as id; pass it to --yes.
Changes things: pass --dry-run to preview, --yes to apply.

Usage:
  linearctl cycle create [flags]

Examples:
  linearctl cycle create --team ENG --starts-at 2026-11-02 --ends-at 2026-11-16 --dry-run --json
  linearctl cycle create --team ENG --starts-at 2026-11-02 --ends-at 2026-11-16 --id 0b6c… --yes

Flags:
      --completed-at TIME   when it was completed, TIME (completes it early)
      --description TEXT    the cycle's description, TEXT
      --dry-run             show what would change; change nothing
      --ends-at TIME        when it ends, TIME
  -h, --help                help for create
      --id UUID             the new cycle's UUID; required with --yes
      --name NAME           the cycle's custom NAME (Linear shows "Cycle N" without one)
      --starts-at TIME      when it starts, TIME: a date or an RFC 3339 time
      --team KEY            create in team KEY (e.g. ENG)
      --yes                 apply the change
```

## linearctl cycle list

```
List cycles, with the same fields as cycle show's top level. Several of --active,
--next, --previous, --past and --future match any of them.

Fields: id, number, name, description, startsAt, endsAt, completedAt, isActive,
isNext, isPrevious, isPast, isFuture, progress, team

Usage:
  linearctl cycle list [flags]

Examples:
  linearctl cycle list --team ENG --json

Flags:
      --active              only the active cycle (Linear's isActive; CYCLE current elsewhere)
      --cursor CURSOR       continue after CURSOR (nextCursor from the previous page)
      --ends-before WHEN    only cycles ending at or before WHEN
      --fields FIELDS       return only these comma-separated FIELDS (see Fields above)
      --future              only cycles yet to start (isFuture)
  -h, --help                help for list
      --limit N             show at most N items; 0 for all (default 50)
      --next                only the next cycle (isNext)
      --past                only cycles that have ended (isPast)
      --previous            only the previous cycle (isPrevious)
      --starts-since WHEN   only cycles starting at or after WHEN (a date, RFC 3339, 7d, 24h)
      --team KEY            only team KEY (falls back to LINEARCTL_TEAM, then default-team)
```

## linearctl cycle show

```
Show a cycle with Linear's own fields: dates, the is* states, progress (completed
points plus a quarter of in-progress ones, over all points), currentProgress, and the
day-by-day histories behind Linear's burndown charts. Nothing is computed here.
CYCLE is current, next, previous, a cycle number, or its UUID; all but a UUID are
per team, so --team (or LINEARCTL_TEAM, or default-team) picks it, and a word that
fits cycles in two teams is an error naming both.
issues and uncompletedIssuesUponClose come as lists: --cursor continues issues,
and --all-issues reads every one, 250 a request.

Fields: id, number, name, description, startsAt, endsAt, completedAt, isActive,
isNext, isPrevious, isPast, isFuture, progress, team, createdAt, updatedAt,
archivedAt, autoArchivedAt, currentProgress, progressHistory, scopeHistory,
completedScopeHistory, inProgressScopeHistory, issueCountHistory,
completedIssueCountHistory, inheritedFrom, issues, uncompletedIssuesUponClose

Usage:
  linearctl cycle show CYCLE [flags]

Examples:
  linearctl cycle show current --team ENG --json
  linearctl cycle show 23 --team ENG --issues 250 --fields number,progress,issues --json
  linearctl cycle show current --team ENG --all-issues --fields number,issues --json

Flags:
      --all-issues      include every issue, however many (overrides --issues)
      --cursor CURSOR   continue after CURSOR (nextCursor from the previous page)
      --fields FIELDS   return only these comma-separated FIELDS (see Fields above)
  -h, --help            help for show
      --issues N        include the first N issues; 0 for none (default 50)
      --team KEY        the cycle's team KEY (falls back to LINEARCTL_TEAM, then default-team)
      --uncompleted N   include the first N issues left open at close; 0 for none (default 50)
```

## linearctl cycle update

```
Change a cycle's name, description or dates. Only what differs is sent; when
nothing does, nothing is sent and the result is changed: false. CYCLE is as for cycle
show, within --team.
Changes things: pass --dry-run to preview, --yes to apply.

Usage:
  linearctl cycle update CYCLE [flags]

Examples:
  linearctl cycle update current --team ENG --name "Checkout v2" --dry-run --json
  linearctl cycle update 24 --team ENG --ends-at 2026-11-05 --yes

Flags:
      --completed-at TIME   when it was completed, TIME (completes it early)
      --description TEXT    the cycle's description, TEXT
      --dry-run             show what would change; change nothing
      --ends-at TIME        when it ends, TIME
  -h, --help                help for update
      --name NAME           the cycle's custom NAME (Linear shows "Cycle N" without one)
      --starts-at TIME      when it starts, TIME: a date or an RFC 3339 time
      --team KEY            the cycle's team KEY (falls back to LINEARCTL_TEAM, then default-team)
      --yes                 apply the change
```
